subject: Atlas routing POC — control/data plane orientation and acceptance checklist
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@atlashealth.io>

Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@atlashealth.io>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: routing POC for Atlas private VPC (control/data split)

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for agreeing to run the short routing POC with Atlas. We want to validate two things over the next two weeks:

1) Clear demarcation and routing for the control plane (management, agent heartbeats, control APIs) vs the data plane (inference egress, model fetch, telemetry).
2) Proof that our onsite egress proxies and Atlas firewall rules can be configured without impacting inference tail latency for 512-token requests.

I've attached a short kickoff agenda and the high-level questions the security team has.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can you share the diagram you expect us to validate against? (control/data subnets, NAT/Egress points, TLS termination expectations)
- A short acceptance checklist we can run with our network team during the window.

Priya from Atlas will be coordinating network access and a brief maintenance window on Thursday (Apr 15).

Thanks,
Tom

--
Tom Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering, Atlas Health Systems

Subject: Re: Kickoff: routing POC for Atlas private VPC (control/data split)

Hi Tom —

Appreciate the clear scope. Short answers up front:
- We'll validate the control plane on a management subnet with pinned egress through your control NAT (no public egress).
- Data plane traffic (inference tokens, model pulls) will flow out the tenant egress proxy; we expect a transparent TLS pass-through for model shards unless we coordinate trusted certs.

Attached: a working diagram (low-fi) and a baseline acceptance checklist (spreadsheet) for the Thursday maintenance window. Soojin will lead the test plan and run the latency scripts from your staging cluster.

Plan proposal:
- Wed Apr 14: configuration sync & dry run (no maintenance window) — validate routes, BGP prefixes, and MTU settings.
- Thu Apr 15: maintenance window — run the acceptance checklist and 1-hour injection of synthetic requests (512-token, multimodal disabled).
- Fri Apr 16: short readout with timings, traces, and failure cases.

Can you confirm the maintenance window time and the contact for Atlas on-site network ops?

Best,
Rachel

Subject: Re: Kickoff: routing POC for Atlas private VPC (control/data split) — test plan and diagrams

Tom / Rachel / Priya —

I've sketched a slightly more concrete runbook and a diagram attached (routing-poc-diagram-20270412.v1.png). Key technical notes for Atlas network team to validate before the dry run:

- MTU: Ensure jumbo frames are not blocked between tenant pods and the egress proxy; set MTU >= 1500 and confirm no path MTU blackhole. We saw subtle latency spikes when MTU mismatches caused fragmentation on long model pulls.
- TCP keepalive vs UDP health checks: control-plane heartbeats use long-lived TLS websockets; keep TCP idle timers > 90s to avoid spurious rekey gaps.
- BGP/Static routes: For the POC, a static route from tucked control subnet to control NAT is sufficient; production should use BGP with route reflectors.
- TLS expectations: Redwood will not terminate customer TLS for model fetches in this POC. If Atlas prefers Redwood-controlled certs, we need to exchange SANs and CA trust ahead of deploy.

Testing tasks (covered in poc-acceptance-checklist.xlsx):
- Task 1: Verify control-plane agent registration while data-plane egress is blocked (simulate misconfigured ACLs).
- Task 2: Run 10k synthetic inference requests (512 tokens) over 1 hour and capture p50/p95/p99 latencies and token throughput.
- Task 3: Induce an egress failover (flip proxy A -> proxy B) and measure tail latency and error rates.

Attachments included in the email: routing-poc-diagram-20270412.v1.png (diagram), poc-acceptance-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), and a short script we use for latency injection (referenced via Drive link).

Notes: Rachel and I will be on call during the maintenance window. Jonas will watch the observability dashboard and validate KV cache warm/warm-up times. Marissa will collect the audit evidence for any control-plane auths (logs, TLS handshakes).

Soojin

--
Soojin Lee

Subject: Re: Kickoff: routing POC for Atlas private VPC (control/data split) — acceptance criteria and next steps

Quick wrap from our side after today's dry-run notes:

- Dry run observations (Wed Apr 14): control-plane agent registrations successful; a small MTU mismatch on path -> corrected by Atlas ops (verified). Data-plane synthetic requests baseline p50=28ms p95=135ms p99=420ms for 512-token window — within our expected envelope for the staging cluster.
- Two follow-ups before Thu's maintenance window:
  1) Atlas to confirm the exact start time for the maintenance window (we recommend 02:00-04:00 UTC to reduce production traffic impact).
  2) Priya to provide the on-site ops phone number and the expected NAT gateway failover method (BGP flap or API-driven route switch).

Acceptance criteria ( short list pulled into poc-acceptance-checklist.xlsx ):
- Control-plane: agent registration + TLS auth logged with no >5% auth error rate during test window.
- Data-plane: p95 latency increase < 40% vs baseline and error rate < 0.5% for synthetic traffic.
- Observability: traces for at least 95% of synthetic requests; KV cache warm-up documented and < 20s for common shards.

Marissa will collect the evidence bundle and upload to the Drive folder linked below after the Thursday run. If you can confirm the maintenance window start time and the contact, we will finalize the runbook and share a short on-call rotation for the two hours.

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bAtlasRoutingPOC
JIRA ticket we will attach evidence to: INFRA-4321

Thanks all — looking forward to the run tomorrow.

Jonas
